item.title: Soccer-Kuyt to take charge of Fenerbahce on interim basis
item.description: Former Liverpool striker Dirk Kuyt will take charge of Fenerbahce on an interim basis following Ismail Kartal's resignation, the Super Lig club said on Wednesday. Kartal departed on Tuesday in ...
item.content:encoded:
Soccer-Kuyt to take charge of Fenerbahce on interim basis Reuters | Updated: 28-10-2026 14:17 IST | Created: 28-10-2026 14:17 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Former Liverpool striker Dirk Kuyt will take charge of Fenerbahce on an interim basis following Ismail Kartal's resignation, the Super Lig club said on Wednesday. Kartal departed on Tuesday in the wake of Fenerbahce's 2-1 defeat at bitter rivals Galatasaray. Kuyt played more than 200 games for Liverpool before moving to Fenerbahce in 2012, winning the Turkish league title two years later. The Dutchman previously coached Belgian side Beerschot as well as ADO Den Haag and FC Dordrecht in the Netherlands, before joining Fenerbahce as assistant coach under Kartal in June. "Following Ismail Kartal's resignation, our club has assigned Dirk Kuyt as the technical supervisor of our Football A team until our new head coach is determined," Fenerbahce said in a statement. Fenerbahce are fifth in the league, six points behind leaders Galatasaray.

item.title: Pakistan fails to protect children as online sexual abuse cases remain underreported, warns HRCP
item.description: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) has raised concerns over the growing threat of online sexual exploitation of children, warning that widespread underreporting, poor coordination among ...
item.content:encoded:
Pakistan fails to protect children as online sexual abuse cases remain underreported, warns HRCP The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) has raised concerns over the growing threat of online sexual exploitation of children, warning that widespread underreporting, poor coordination among institutions and inadequate protective measures continue to hinder efforts to tackle the problem, as reported by The Express Tribune. ANI | Updated: 28-10-2026 13:27 IST | Created: 28-10-2026 13:27 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) has raised concerns over the growing threat of online sexual exploitation of children, warning that widespread underreporting, poor coordination among institutions and inadequate protective measures continue to hinder efforts to tackle the problem, as reported by The Express Tribune. According to The Express Tribune, in a report, HRCP said online child sexual abuse should not be viewed solely as a cybercrime issue but as a serious violation of children's fundamental rights, dignity and personal safety. Highlighting the scale of the problem, the report cited a 2025 case in Muzaffargarh, where at least 50 children, including those aged six or younger, were allegedly exploited through an international network. Figures from the US-based National Center for Missing and Exploited Children showed that reports concerning suspected child sexual abuse material linked to Pakistan crossed two million in 2021. The HRCP clarified that these figures reflected reports of suspected online activity and did not represent the number of individual victims. The commission urged authorities to improve coordination between child protection agencies, police, cybercrime investigators, prosecutors and courts to strengthen investigations and ensure perpetrators are held accountable. It also stressed that affected children must have access to legal assistance, psychological counselling and rehabilitation services. According to the HRCP, awareness campaigns alone cannot address the crisis without stronger protection systems, institutional accountability and greater responsibility from digital platforms. The commission called for a comprehensive response that prioritises children's safety while ensuring that existing legal and institutional mechanisms are implemented effectively, as cited by The Express Tribune. The warning comes amid further evidence of the scale of online abuse in Pakistan. A separate report launched in September by the National Commission on the Rights of the Child, in collaboration with UNICEF Pakistan, estimated that approximately 1.5 million Pakistani children aged 12 to 17 who used the internet experienced online sexual exploitation and abuse within a single year, as reported by The Express Tribune. (ANI)

item.title: Attack at Balochistan Nushki Girls’ College leaves 3 injured, raising alarm over campus safety
item.description: Three female students were injured after armed, masked men stormed a girls’ degree college in Nushki district, raising concerns over the security of educational institutions in Balochistan, as ...
item.content:encoded:
Attack at Balochistan Nushki Girls’ College leaves 3 injured, raising alarm over campus safety  Three female students were injured after armed, masked men stormed a girls’ degree college in Nushki district, raising concerns over the security of educational institutions in Balochistan, as reported by The Balochistan Post. ANI | Updated: 28-10-2026 12:33 IST | Created: 28-10-2026 12:33 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Three female students were injured after armed, masked men stormed a girls’ degree college in Nushki district, raising concerns over the security of educational institutions in Balochistan, as reported by The Balochistan Post. According to The Balochistan Post, the college administration said that three gunmen entered the premises, damaged surveillance cameras, vandalised the principal’s office and opened fire on students. The injured, identified as Mehmoona, Maryam and Rukhsana, were taken to Mir Gul Khan Naseer Teaching Hospital. Rukhsana was later referred to Quetta due to the seriousness of her injuries. The attackers’ motive remained unclear. The Baloch Students Action Committee (BSAC) condemned the incident, warning that repeated attacks on educational institutions were creating fear among students and undermining education. Its spokesperson noted that teachers and professors had previously been targeted, with students now facing similar violence. The organisation demanded immediate action, justice for the victims and accountability for those responsible. BSAC chairman Uzair Baloch also denounced the shooting, arguing that educational institutions were being targeted to obstruct education in the region. Journalist Bahot Baloch described the attack as an alleged conspiracy to prevent Baloch women from accessing education. He questioned how the gunmen escaped despite security installations reportedly located near the college. The shooting follows another attack on Ruzhn School in Buleda’s Minaz area, where masked gunmen reportedly fired at surveillance cameras. School authorities said several educational institutions in the region had previously faced similar incidents. In Panjgur in 2014, a religious group reportedly threatened private schools, demanding the removal of female students or closure, as highlighted by The Balochistan Post. The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan subsequently documented prolonged school closures and sharply reduced attendance following intimidation. Concerns also persist over the safety of educators. Baloch rights organisations have reported the abductions and killings of several teachers, as reported by The Balochistan Post. (ANI)

item.title: Trump approved Flávio Bolsonaro's US entry after Brazil election loss: Reports
item.description: US President Donald Trump approved allowing Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to enter the United States following his defeat in Brazil's presidential election, a Trump adviser told CNN, while ...
item.content:encoded:
Trump approved Flávio Bolsonaro's US entry after Brazil election loss: Reports US President Donald Trump approved allowing Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to enter the United States following his defeat in Brazil's presidential election, a Trump adviser told CNN, while Brazilian news site, Bahia Notícias reported that Washington would grant visas to the senator and his family. ANI | Updated: 28-10-2026 09:43 IST | Created: 28-10-2026 09:43 IST

Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump approved allowing Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to enter the United States following his defeat in Brazil's presidential election, a Trump adviser told CNN, while Brazilian news site, Bahia Notícias reported that Washington would grant visas to the senator and his family. According to CNN, Trump administration officials were aware on Monday (local time) that Bolsonaro had approximately 24 hours to surrender his passport under a Brazilian Supreme Court order and made clear that he would be allowed to enter the United States. Two US officials told CNN that visas were being issued to Bolsonaro and his family. Brazilian news outlet Bahia Notícias, citing information confirmed by a White House official to Folha de S Paulo on Tuesday, also reported that the US government was aware of the senator's trip and would grant visas to the family. According to people close to the Bolsonaro family, the senator arrived in the United States at around 4:20 pm, accompanied by his wife, Fernanda, and their two daughters. His departure came two days after he lost the presidential election to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Brazilian news outlet Bahia Notícias, citing sources familiar with the operation, reported that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was involved in facilitating Bolsonaro's departure. CNN reported that it remained unclear whether Trump and Bolsonaro had spoken directly by phone before the senator left Brazil. The departure followed an order by Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes directing Bolsonaro to surrender his passports within 24 hours. According to CNN, Bolsonaro had denied intending to flee the country in a video posted on Instagram on Monday (local time). CNN reported that the senator is under investigation by Brazil's highest court over alleged corruption, money laundering and currency evasion. The investigations include allegations linked to online betting platforms and the financing of a biopic about his father, former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro. Flávio Bolsonaro denies wrongdoing. CNN reported that no arrest warrant had been issued against him at the time of his departure. Meanwhile, Brazilian President Lula criticised Bolsonaro's reported departure while addressing supporters outside the Palácio da Alvorada on Tuesday (local time), during celebrations marking his 81st birthday. According to Brazilian news outlet Bahia Notícias, Lula called the senator's departure a "shameful act" and said he should have surrendered his passport in compliance with the court's order. "The citizen who leaves their country in secret does so because they owe something," Lula said, according to Brazilian media. Drawing a comparison with his own legal proceedings during Operation Lava Jato, Lula said he had chosen to remain in Brazil and surrender to the Federal Police when he faced accusations. "I decided to turn myself in to the Federal Police because I wanted to unmask my accusers and prove my innocence," Lula said, according to Bahia Notícias. Brazilian news outlet CNN Brasil also reported that Lula criticised Bolsonaro's departure, saying the senator could have remained in the country to address the allegations against him. The reported departure appeared to have surprised members of Bolsonaro's political camp. His campaign manager, Rogerio Marinho, told reporters that the opposition had expected the senator to assume a leadership role after the election. "We're surprised because yesterday we talked about the need for Flávio -- given the roughly 60 million votes he received -- to take on this leadership role for the opposition," Marinho said, according to CNN. The episode follows the departure of Bolsonaro's father, Jair Bolsonaro, for Orlando, Florida, after losing Brazil's 2022 presidential election. Jair Bolsonaro was subsequently sentenced to 27 years in prison over efforts to overturn the election results. Brazilian media reported that Flávio Bolsonaro was expected to address the press on Wednesday (local time), although the location had not been disclosed. (ANI)
